rationale: Two conventions used throughout this file: (1) The task brief's default fn name for the self-check module is 'selfCheckResult'. The actual exported function in lib/rule-engine/selfCheck.ts is `bucketSelfCheck(answers: SelfCheckAnswers): SelfCheckBucket`. All self-check-bucket-level cases below (area 'self-check-bucket', ids CK-*) use fn: 'bucketSelfCheck' accordingly, per the task instructions' own fallback rule. (2) Raw JSON has no `undefined` literal, but several cases need to assert that a result field is genuinely absent/undefined (e.g. `priority` when only 1 code was selected, `deadline` when suppressed, `grievance` when no variant applies at all) rather than an empty object or null. Wherever `expected` contains a field set to JSON `null` (e.g. `"deadline": null`, `"priority": null`, `"grievance": null`), the executor should read this as 'assert the real result's field is `undefined` (absent)', not as a literal `=== null` check — the rule-engine's own TypeScript types never actually assign `null` to these fields, only `undefined` (optional/absent). Also note: array-valued fields in `expected` (entries, issueEntries, issues, tier1/tier2/unranked/ranked, unsureItems, missing, errors) are intended to be matched by their given per-element keys only where each element is itself a partial object (e.g. `{code: "CODE_2_DOE"}` should match a real entry that also carries `explanation`/`fix` text) — but the ARRAY itself (length and order) must match exactly, per the task instructions' own array-exact-match rule.

3-day deadline (KYC complete at filing) for a claim filed 2026-08-01 is 2026-08-04. Spec Section 5 pseudocode uses `<=` for the NOT_YET_DUE branch, and ticket 03's own 'Done means' explicitly requires the exact-boundary date to be NOT_YET_DUE, not MISSED.
One calendar day before the 3-day deadline (2026-08-04) must still read as on time, with exactly 1 day remaining. Rule Engine Spec.md Section 5.
One calendar day after the 3-day deadline (2026-08-04) must read as missed by exactly 1 day. Rule Engine Spec.md Section 5.
20-day deadline (KYC not complete) for a claim filed 2026-08-01 is 2026-08-21. Exact-boundary day must be NOT_YET_DUE per Spec Section 5's `<=` rule.
One day before the 20-day boundary (2026-08-21) — still on time, 1 day remaining.
One day after the 20-day boundary (2026-08-21) — missed by exactly 1 day.
Reference date equal to filing date (zero days elapsed) — the full 3-day allowance should still be remaining. Boundary/edge case not explicit in the spec pseudocode but follows directly from it.
Same zero-elapsed-time boundary on the 20-day branch — full allowance remaining.
Month-boundary regression check: filing 2026-01-30 + 3 calendar days crosses into February (Jan has 31 days) and must land on 2026-02-02, still NOT_YET_DUE on the exact boundary.

Large-miss regression: 20-day deadline from 2026-01-01 is 2026-01-21; checked against 2026-03-01 (39 calendar days later, verified via calendar arithmetic: 10 remaining days in Jan + 28 days in Feb 2026 (non-leap) + 1 day into March = 39). Confirms the calendar-day (not working-day) assumption from Spec Section 5/9-gap-6 compounds correctly over a long gap.

`basis` must be threaded straight through into the result unchanged, tagging this MISSED result as a confirmed-fact rejection date (deadline.ts's own DeadlineBasis doc comment, and today's rejection_date change).
Identical math to DL-011 but tagged basis='today' — proves `basis` only labels the result, it never changes the day-count math itself.

Adversarial/robustness case: a reference date before the filing date (schema.ts's own rejection_date<filing_date guard prevents this for rejection_date, but a stale/skewed 'today' clock could still produce it). checkDeadline is a pure function with no guard of its own, so it should still degrade gracefully to NOT_YET_DUE with a larger-than-normal daysRemaining rather than throw or produce a negative count.

Leap-year regression: 2028 is a leap year (Feb has 29 days). 20 calendar days from 2028-02-10 must land on 2028-03-01 exactly, still NOT_YET_DUE on the boundary — verified independently via calendar arithmetic.

Rule Engine Spec.md Section 5: the H11 deadline check is suppressed entirely for Code 8, even when a rejection_date is supplied — an ineligible claim was never going to be settled regardless of the clock, so the check must not silently reappear just because a rejection_date is now known.
Same suppression without a rejection_date at all (basis='today' would otherwise apply) — Code 8 must suppress regardless of which basis would have been used.

Rule Engine Spec.md Section 5 (ticket 17): Code 9 (wrong form filed) suppresses the deadline check too, even with a rejection_date supplied — a claim filed under the wrong form was never going to be settled under that form regardless of the clock.
Same Code 9 suppression without a rejection_date at all.

A non-suppressed code (Code 2) with a known rejection_date: the deadline is evaluated against the rejection date (EPFO's act of settling the claim), not against today — 20-day deadline is 2026-08-21, rejected 2026-08-25 is 4 calendar days late (verified via calendar arithmetic).

Same code/dates but no rejection_date given: the check falls back to today_date as the reference and must be tagged basis='today' — an as-of-today estimate, not a confirmed fact (today's change to deadline.ts/index.ts).

Boundary: rejection_date equal to filing_date is a legal, schema-allowed value (schema.ts only rejects rejection_date < filing_date, not ==). Zero days elapsed means the full 20-day allowance is still remaining.

Rule Engine Spec.md Section 3, Code 10: unlike Codes 8/9, Code 10 is NOT in DEADLINE_SUPPRESSED_CODES — EPFO gave a real (if unrecognized) reason, so the claim was not inherently unsettleable and the deadline check must run normally.
Rule Engine Spec.md Section 3, Code 1: 'not_verified' routes to the standard-mismatch branch (Joint Declaration fix). entries array matched by code+meta.branch only, not full explanation/fix text.

Spec Section 3, Code 1: 'unsure' defaults to the less-severe standard-mismatch branch, not the portal-sync-bug branch — same default-to-less-severe pattern the spec uses elsewhere (e.g. Code 3's bank_account_type unsure).
Spec Section 3, Code 1: 'approved_and_verified' means the KYC page already shows the detail as correct — this is the portal-sync-bug branch (do not file a Joint Declaration).

Rule Engine Spec.md Section 3, Code 3 (ticket 15): a joint account is a hard rejection independent of timing, checked before the wait-time bands — it wins even when a submission date happens to be present, since the fix has nothing to do with waiting longer.

Working days strictly between 2026-08-24 (Mon) and 2026-08-31 (Mon), Mon-Fri only, excluding the weekend of Aug 29-30: Aug 25,26,27,28,31 = 5 working days — the upper boundary of Band 1 (0-5 days, spec Section 3 Code 3 table). Verified independently via calendar weekday lookup.
One working day later than D3-002 (6 working days) crosses into Band 2's lower boundary (6-10 days).
10 working days between 2026-08-24 and 2026-09-07 (verified via calendar weekday count) is Band 2's upper boundary — still 'worth checking, not yet clearly stuck', not yet an escalation.

One working day past D3-004's boundary (11 working days) crosses into Band 3 (more than 10 days) — 'well beyond the typical turnaround, worth escalating' per spec Section 3, generates Variant B grievance eligibility.
Spec Section 2: `bank_account_type: unsure` routes to the normal wait-time-band flow, not the joint-account branch — same result as the 'individual' case (D3-002) with identical dates.

Weekend edge case: submission on a Saturday (2026-08-22), checked the very next day, a Sunday (2026-08-23) — the working-days-between window (exclusive of submission day) contains only a Sunday, so workingDays=0, still Band 1. Exercises waitBands.ts's Mon-Fri-only counting at a weekend boundary.
Spec Section 3, Code 8 (ticket 16): under-6-months branch — genuine eligibility rule, wait and refile Form 10C.
Spec Section 3, Code 8: over-9.5-years branch — routes to Form 10D pension claim instead of Form 10C lump sum.
Spec Section 3, Code 8: 'unsure' is a real third branch (not a default) since the two known thresholds have opposite remedies — guessing wrong would send the citizen down the wrong fix.
Spec Section 3, Code 9 (ticket 17): full-settlement intent maps to Form 19.
Spec Section 3, Code 9: pension-only intent maps to Form 10C.
Spec Section 3, Code 9: advance-while-employed intent maps to Form 31.
Spec Section 3, Code 9: 'unsure' is a real fourth branch since many citizens don't clearly distinguish 'my PF' from 'my EPS/pension' and a wrong guess recommends the wrong form.

Code 4 (EPS discrepancy) has no branching — a single explanation/fix pair per spec Section 3.
Code 5 (old claim pending) has no branching — a single explanation/fix pair per spec Section 3.

Code 6 (approved but not credited) has no branching — a single explanation/fix pair per spec Section 3. diagnose() itself has no exclusivity enforcement (that lives in schema.ts), so it structurally supports resolving Code 6 alone.
Spec Section 3, Code 7: every check passing in its pass direction (note old_claim_pending's polarity flip — 'no' is the pass answer) yields the 'all clean' outcome that generates Variant E.
A single issue (Date of Exit not marked) routes to Code 2's explanation/fix, per spec Section 3's self-check routing table.

Two issues, deliberately given in reverse-of-checklist input relevance (old_claim_pending is checklist item 5, doe_marked is item 1): issueEntries must come back in the checklist's own fixed order (selfCheck.ts's SELF_CHECK_MAPPING order), not any input-dependent order — index.ts relies on this fixed order to pick 'the first issue found' as the grievance subject.

Spec Section 3, Code 7 footnote: the bank-KYC self-check item only confirms verification status, collects no submission date, so it must resolve to CODE_3_GENERAL text with NO band/meta at all — not a wait-time band. The issueEntries[0] object should have no `meta` key (band or branch).

Regression case for the 2026-09-02 source-link audit fix noted in diagnose.ts's resolveSelfCheckIssueCode: a self-check-routed Code 1 issue must carry meta.branch='standard_mismatch' (not omit meta entirely) so hasBranch()/sourcesFor() correctly show the Joint Declaration + UAN portal citation rather than silently misreading it as the portal-sync-bug branch. This is exactly the bug the audit found and fixed — a strong regression case.
Spec Section 3, Code 7: an 'unsure' answer must not be treated as clean — allClean stays false and the item is surfaced for double-checking, distinct from a real issue (issueEntries stays empty).

Spec Section 3, Code 10 (ticket 10): shares Code 7's self-check mechanics exactly — the bucketing logic is code-agnostic, only the downstream grievance/UI copy differs (Variant F vs E). Confirms Code 10 alone triggers the identical self-check branch in diagnose().
Spec Section 4 pseudocode: size(selected) <= 1 needs no ranking at all.
Empty selection — degenerate input, must not throw and must report no ranking needed.

Spec Section 4 decision table: 'Both Code 2 and Code 5 selected — no source-stated order between these two Tier 1 codes.' The implementation preserves input/selection order for tier1 (no defined order per spec), which this case documents explicitly.

Spec Section 4: 'Both Code 1 and Code 3 selected -> Fix Code 3 (Bank KYC) first, then Code 1.' Deliberately given in the OPPOSITE order ([CODE_1, CODE_3]) to prove tier2 is force-reordered regardless of selection order — the source finding states Bank KYC must always rank above Name/DOB.
Spec Section 4 decision table: 'Any one of Code 2 or Code 5, plus any one of Code 1 or Code 3 -> fix the Tier 1 code first (eligibility), then the Tier 2 code (payment).'

All 5 diagnosable codes together — the full pseudocode from spec Section 4: tier1 in selection order, tier2 force-ordered (Bank KYC before Name/DOB), Code 4 kept unranked and excluded from `ranked` entirely (shown separately, no implied rank per spec Section 9 gap 4).
Spec Section 4 decision table: 'Code 4 selected alongside any other code -> show Code 4's explanation/fix separately, without claiming a priority rank.' Code 4 must never appear in `ranked`.

Single-code selection needs no priority ranking (spec Section 4). Code 4 alone still gets a normal Variant A grievance (spec Section 6 lists Code 4 among Variant A's codes) and a normal deadline check.

Tier1-tie case: spec Section 4 explicitly says Code 2 and Code 5 have 'no source-stated order... unranked relative to each other,' yet index.ts's grievance generator must still pick ONE primary code for the single auto-generated grievance (an MVP simplification, spec Section 6 is silent on multi-code grievances). This case documents that the implementation's tie-break is selection-input order (CODE_5 selected first here, so it wins) — a real, worth-flagging design gap since the spec doesn't define this order and a citizen who happens to click the two checkboxes in the other order gets a different grievance subject for the exact same situation. [UPDATED 2026-09-02, ticket 19: the tie-break itself (which of the two wins the single `grievance` slot) is unchanged and still input-order-dependent — but this is now cosmetic rather than a real gap, since CODE_2's own grievance is no longer silently dropped: it's returned in additionalGrievances instead. See Engineering/tickets/19-multi-code-grievance-suppression.md.]

Bank KYC (band 1, only 5 working days elapsed — see D3-002) outranks Name/DOB mismatch per spec Section 4, but Band 1 itself is explicitly not_applicable for a grievance (spec Section 6, 'For Bands 1 and 2, no grievance is generated'). [RESOLVED 2026-09-02, ticket 19: this used to mean the citizen got NO grievance at all — the not_applicable Bank KYC result silently discarded the Name/DOB mismatch's own valid Variant A grievance. Fixed in index.ts: a not_applicable code is now skipped when picking the primary, so Name/DOB's Variant A is promoted instead. additionalGrievances is empty here since Bank KYC's not_applicable result is excluded entirely rather than surfaced as a dead slot. SPEC-GAP tag removed — this is no longer an open gap, see Engineering/tickets/19-multi-code-grievance-suppression.md for the resolution.]

Full 3-tier combination (Tier1 + Tier2 pair + a rich branch on the non-primary code). Tier1's single code (CODE_2_DOE) outranks both Tier2 codes and becomes the grievance primary (Variant A for Code 2), even though Code 1 resolved to the richer portal-sync-bug branch (which would itself be Variant C) — proving priority order, not branch richness, drives grievance selection. `diagnosis.entries` order matches `rejection_codes_selected`'s selection order, not priority order (Wizard.tsx re-sorts for display, the API itself does not).

Unranked Code 4 alongside a single Tier1 code: the grievance primary must be the ranked code (Code 2), never the unranked one, per index.ts's `priority?.ranked[0] ?? diagnosableSelected[0]` fallback logic — Code 4 is excluded from `ranked` so it can never win this fallback while a ranked code is present.

Code 6 is exclusive (not in DiagnosableCode) so no priority ranking applies, and it is NOT in DEADLINE_SUPPRESSED_CODES — spec Section 5 only suppresses Codes 8/9, so the deadline check still runs normally for Code 6. Grievance: Variant D per spec Section 6.
Spec Section 6, Code 8: no grievance for any branch — a genuine eligibility rule can't be overridden by a grievance. Deadline is also suppressed (Section 5).

Ticket 17's second code-review pass fix: `not_applicable` is checked BEFORE `missing_info` in buildGrievance() — even with uan/claim_id both entirely absent, the reason must still be `not_applicable`, never `missing_info`. This is the exact regression the ticket fixed (a misleading 'still needs your UAN' intermediate state).
Same not_applicable-before-missing_info precedence check as PF-008, for Code 9 this time — spec Section 6: 'the fix is refiling under the correct form, not something to escalate with EPFO.'

Joint-account rejection (ticket 15) with uan/claim_id both absent: grievance must still resolve to not_applicable (same precedence fix as PF-008/009, applying to Code 3's joint branch too), while the deadline check still runs normally since Code 3 is not in DEADLINE_SUPPRESSED_CODES.
Standard-mismatch Code 1 alone maps to Variant A (spec Section 6 lists Code 1's standard branch among Variant A's codes).
Portal-sync-bug Code 1 branch maps to Variant C, a distinct grievance template from the standard branch (spec Section 6, Variant C).

All self-checks clean under Code 7 generates the 'demand the real reason' Variant E grievance (spec Section 3/6), and spec Section 9 gap-10's clarification confirms the deadline check still runs on this path (it is NOT a dead end that skips straight past it).

Two issues found (Date of Exit + EPS); spec Section 9 gap-10: the FIRST issue in the checklist's fixed order (Date of Exit, CODE_2) is the grievance subject — 'using the first issue found (in the checklist's fixed order) as the subject when more than one issue is found.'

Spec Section 9 gap-10 / index.ts's kindForSelfCheckIssue: when the ONLY self-check issue found is bank KYC (Code 3), no grievance variant applies — no submission date was collected in this context, so there's no wait-time band to justify Variant B, and Variant A never covers Code 3. `grievance` must be entirely absent, not an object with reason='not_applicable'.

Domain correctness: an unsure-only self-check result means the citizen has NOT actually ruled out the common causes, so generating Variant E's 'I have checked my own records... and found no issue' text would be false. The implementation correctly requires allClean (issueEntries AND unsureItems both empty) before offering Variant E — an unsure-only result must produce no grievance at all.

Spec Section 3, Code 10: all self-checks clean generates Variant F ('demand clarification'), distinct from Code 7's Variant E, and the deadline check runs normally (Code 10 is not in DEADLINE_SUPPRESSED_CODES, unlike Codes 8/9).

Code 10's self-check issue-found path uses the exact same kindForSelfCheckIssue mechanics as Code 7 (spec Section 3, Code 10: 'The bucketing logic is code-agnostic; only the downstream copy differs from Code 7') — a real issue still routes to a normal Variant A grievance, not Variant F.

Adversarial/defensive test: this combination is invalid per schema.ts (both codes are mutually exclusive) and would never reach runPostRejectionFlow() through the real API — but the orchestrator has its own documented internal guarantee (index.ts's EXCLUSIVE_CODE_GRIEVANCE_KIND, iterated in fixed key order Code 6 -> 8 -> 9) that Code 6 always wins if a caller ever bypasses validation. This tests that the orchestrator's own stated invariant holds; also confirms the deadline suppression check (`.some()` over all selected codes) fires from Code 8's mere presence even though Code 6 'wins' the grievance.
Band 2 (7 working days between 2026-08-24 and 2026-09-02, verified via calendar weekday count) — spec Section 6: 'For Bands 1 and 2, no grievance is generated.'

Band 3 (well over 10 working days between 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-08) generates a ready Variant B grievance per spec Section 6, combined with a MISSED 3-day deadline (deadline 2026-08-04, rejected 2026-08-20, 16 calendar days late) that should also get cited in the grievance body (deadlineCited).
MISSED deadline (confirmed via rejection_date) must be cited in the grievance body (spec Section 6's deadline citation block, `deadlineCited: true`).
NOT_YET_DUE (basis='today', no rejection_date given) must NOT get a deadline citation appended — only a MISSED status triggers the citation block, regardless of basis.

MISSED via the 'today' fallback (no rejection_date known) must still cite the deadline in the grievance — but the citation text must be hedged (conditional 'if my rejection was issued after X'), not asserted as settled fact, since 'today' is only a stand-in for the real decision date. See the grievance-area cases (GR-015) and 'Suspected existing bugs' for a specific wording concern with this exact basis.

Boundary: rejection_date equal to filing_date is schema-legal (only < is rejected) — zero days elapsed, full 20-day allowance remaining, at the runPostRejectionFlow integration level (duplicate-but-distinct from DS-007's more narrowly-scoped assertion).
